properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 8 at 1:43AM CDT until July 8 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
FFWABR

The National Weather Service in Aberdeen has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Brown County in northeastern South Dakota...

* Until 800 AM CDT Wednesday.

* At 143 AM CDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3.5
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported. City of Aberdeen employee
reports vehicles stalled due to water and multiple street
completely underwater, at least a foot deep.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Aberdeen and Bath.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

possible.

Locations impacted include...
Hammond and Boyes.
properties.instruction:

weather conditions.

properties.description:

miles north of Cometa, or 15 miles southwest of La Pryor, moving
north at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Uvalde, Crystal City, Brackettville, Spofford, La Pryor, Chula
Vista-River Spur, Blewett, Washer, Las Colonias, Uvalde Estates,

properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.
